name: NC-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +17 partisan lean
Incumbent Deborah Ross running with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger is minimally funded and unknown
Markets price Ross at ~94% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively to Ross: a +17 Democratic district, incumbency, and a fundraising edge of roughly $1.7 million raised against a Republican with no reported finances. Prediction markets price her near-certain to win, and no polls or ratings suggest any threat.
model.watch: A surprise outside-spending surge for the Republican challenger would be the only realistic way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Deborah Ross, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Raleigh-area district drawn firmly for her party, with a partisan lean of about 17 points Democratic. She enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised about $1.7 million and holding over $1.3 million on hand, while Republican Eugene Douglass reports no fundraising activity and no outside groups are engaged on either side.

No public polling covers the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Ross roughly a 94% chance of winning. The forecast treats the seat as safely Democratic, with the incumbent expected to win by a margin in the low-to-mid twenties.
